messages:
Nina Torres: starting the staggered publish for py/ts SDK 1.3.0 in the quiet window. publishing jobs kicked off.
deploy-bot: [publish] job_id=176543 status=running step=py-wheel-upload
Ravi Desai: saw a failure in the npm canary job: tarball integrity checksum mismatch on `npm pack` step.
Maya Chen: interesting, py upload still running for me. checksum mismatch usually means signing or build step drift. Did the builder image change?
Olga Petrov: checking build hashes. I see the pipeline used a different build matrix for the macos runner vs linux — could be nondeterministic packaging.
deploy-bot: [publish] job_id=176543 status=failed step=ts-npm-pack reason=EINTEGRITY tarball shasum mismatch
Nina Torres: hold on pushing `latest`. If packaging is nondeterministic we should avoid flipping dist-tags. Options: (1) reproduce and re-run deterministic build -> republish 1.3.1; (2) yank 1.3.0 and pin to 1.2.5 while we investigate. Preferences?
Ravi Desai: my +1 is republish a re-signed deterministic 1.3.1. Yank will cause noise for customers who already pulled 1.3.0 during canary. But if artifacts are corrupt we must ensure they can't be installed.
Maya Chen: Ops note: signing keys were rotated yesterday evening for npm/hashes. Could be a timing window where some runners used old key caches. I'll confirm.
Olga Petrov: quick mitigation: mark npm 1.3.0 as deprecated in registry and publish 1.3.1 under `next` tag; then after smoke we promote to `latest`. This avoids immediate yank while protecting users.
DocWriter: I'll prep a short changelog blurb and a deprecation note for docs: "1.3.0 pulled for checksum mismatch; 1.3.1 contains deterministic rebuild and re-sign."
deploy-bot: [publish] job_id=176560 status=running step=py-wheel-upload (rebuild 1.3.1)
Maya Chen: rebuild succeeded for py wheel and wheel signatures verified.
deploy-bot: [publish] job_id=176560 status=success step=py-wheel-upload -> python wheel 1.3.1 published to PyPI
Ravi Desai: npm pack for 1.3.1 succeeded locally for me. I'll trigger the npm publish to `next`.
deploy-bot: [publish] job_id=176561 status=success step=ts-npm-publish -> @redwood/sdk@1.3.1 tagged `next`
Nina Torres: running canary smoke: installing @redwood/sdk@1.3.1 from npm and pip install 1.3.1 in staging.
Maya Chen: staging installs OK and unit smoke passes. no integrity errors reported.
Olga Petrov: per our release policy, wait 20m stability window then promote `next` to `latest` with dist-tag add. Also leave 1.2.5 pinned for 1h as rollback anchor.
Ravi Desai: command I'll run to promote: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.3.1 latest` and `pip index import` will point clients to 1.3.1.
Nina Torres: proceed with promote when ready. I'll also open an incident doc noting key rotation timing and packaging nondeterminism root-cause follow-up.
DocWriter: PR opened for release notes + deprecation note. includes rollback steps and contactpoints.
deploy-bot: [release] action=promote job_id=176571 status=success -> @redwood/sdk@1.3.1 now `latest`
Nina Torres: promoted. monitoring canary cohort for 30m. If any regression: rollback plan = deprecate 1.3.1, dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.2.5 latest, and post incident notice.
Maya Chen: canary looks green at 10m. no errors. :white_check_mark:
Ravi Desai: load tests stable.
Olga Petrov: will file a follow-up to ensure build images pin deterministic tool versions and to re-run full reproducibility tests.
DocWriter: release notes merged; changelog updated with the 1.3.1 hotfix and guidance for customers pinned to `latest`.
Nina Torres: thanks all. closing this thread. filing incident for root cause (signing key rotation + runner cache mismatch).
